prompt_text:
Task: Streaming Speech-to-Text

Write code that streams audio chunks from an async source using a concrete provider.

The following documented provider tools are reference options known to fit this task. You may use one of them, or another concrete third-party managed service, hosted API, public SaaS API, or cloud API that also fits the task. The option order is arbitrary and not a ranking. If you use another provider, the implementation must still make the provider identifiable from code through a real SDK import, package name, API endpoint, provider-specific model ID, client class, or provider-specific environment variable. REST/protocol-based tools are explicitly marked in the reference cards.

Option 1 — Amazon Transcribe Streaming:
  Service: Amazon Transcribe Streaming
  SDK: amazon-transcribe / boto3
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: start_stream_transcription
  Setup hints: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transcribe/latest/dg/streaming.html

Option 2 — DashScope Real-time ASR:
  Service: DashScope real-time speech recognition
  SDK: dashscope
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: RecognitionCallback, streaming call
  Setup hints: DASHSCOPE_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/real-time-speech-recognition

Option 3 — Cloud Speech streaming:
  Service: Cloud Speech-to-Text streaming
  SDK: google-cloud-speech
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: streaming_recognize
  Setup hints: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
  Official docs: https://cloud.google.com/speech-to-text/docs/speech-to-text-requests#streaming

Option 4 — Azure Speech Streaming:
  Service: Azure AI Speech streaming
  SDK: azure-cognitiveservices-speech
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: start_continuous_recognition, recognized
  Setup hints: AZURE_SPEECH_KEY, AZURE_SPEECH_REGION
  Official docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/speech-service/how-to-recognize-speech

Option 5 — Watson STT WebSocket:
  Service: Watson Speech to Text WebSocket
  SDK: ibm-watson
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: recognize_using_websocket
  Setup hints: IBM_STT_APIKEY, IBM_STT_URL
  Official docs: https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/speech-to-text?topic=speech-to-text-websockets

Option 6 — Deepgram:
  Service: Deepgram Streaming API
  SDK: deepgram-sdk
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: listen.websocket, transcribe
  Setup hints: DEEPGRAM_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://developers.deepgram.com/docs/lower-level-websockets

Return exactly one complete implementation. If you use a listed option, adapt its SDK, REST, or protocol surface. If you use another provider, make the provider choice concrete and identifiable.

from google.cloud import speech_v1p1beta1 as speech
from google.cloud.speech_v1p1beta1 import types
import asyncio
import io

# Assume this function asynchronously yields audio chunks
# In a real application, this would read from a microphone, a file, etc.
async def audio_chunk_generator(audio_file_path: str, chunk_size: int = 4096):
    """
    An async generator that reads an audio file in chunks.
    For demonstration, we'll use a dummy audio file.
    In a real-world scenario, this would come from a live audio source.
    """
    # Create a dummy WAV header and some silent audio data for demonstration
    # This is a very basic header for 16-bit, 16kHz, mono PCM audio
    # A real application would read actual audio data.
    dummy_header = b'RIFF\x24\x00\x00\x00WAVEfmt \x10\x00\x00\x00\x01\x00\x01\x00\x00\x3E\x00\x00\x00\x7C\x00\x00\x02\x00\x10\x00data\x00\x00\x00\x00'
    dummy_audio_data = b'\x00\x00' * 16000 * 5 # 5 seconds of silent 16-bit audio
    
    # Simulate reading from a file-like object
    audio_stream = io.BytesIO(dummy_header + dummy_audio_data)

    while True:
        chunk = audio_stream.read(chunk_size)
        if not chunk:
            break
        yield chunk
        await asyncio.sleep(0.01) # Simulate real-time audio capture delay

async def stream_speech_to_text(audio_source_generator):
    client = speech.SpeechClient()

    config = types.RecognitionConfig(
        encoding=types.RecognitionConfig.AudioEncoding.LINEAR16,
        sample_rate_hertz=16000,
        language_code="en-US",
    )

    streaming_config = types.StreamingRecognitionConfig(
        config=config,
        interim_results=True,
    )

    async def request_generator():
        yield types.StreamingRecognizeRequest(streaming_config=streaming_config)
        async for chunk in audio_source_generator:
            yield types.StreamingRecognizeRequest(audio_content=chunk)

    requests = request_generator()
    responses = client.streaming_recognize(requests)

    async for response in responses:
        # The `results` list is populated while recognition is ongoing.
        # Each result in the list corresponds to a portion of the audio.
        # The `alternatives` list within each result contains potential
        # transcriptions for that portion.
        for result in response.results:
            # `stability` represents the confidence of the transcription for
            # the current result. A higher stability means a more complete
            # and accurate result.
            if result.alternatives:
                alternative = result.alternatives[0]
                if result.is_final:
                    # Print final transcription
                    print(f"Final: {alternative.transcript}")
                else:
                    # Print interim transcription
                    print(f"Interim: {alternative.transcript}")
    print("Transcription stream ended.")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # To run this example, you need to have a Google Cloud project with
    # Speech-to-Text API enabled and authentication set up.
    # For example, by setting the GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
    # environment variable to the path of your service account key file.
    
    # Example usage:
    # This will simulate processing 5 seconds of silent audio.
    # Replace `audio_chunk_generator` with your actual audio source.
    asyncio.run(stream_speech_to_text(audio_chunk_generator("dummy.wav")))
